{{Short description|American statistician}}

'''Craig A. Hill''' was a research institute executive and a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]]. His research focuses on [[big data]] and the application of new technologies to social science methods.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Craig A. Hill |url=https://www.rti.org/expert/craig-hill |access-date=February 9, 2024 |website=RTI International Experts |date=November 2020 |archive-date=December 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210140727/https://www.rti.org/expert/craig-hill |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
He received his Ph.D. and M.A. in political science from the [[University of New Orleans]]<ref name=":0" /> and has published and presented more than 50 papers,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Craig A. Hill |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hLihO0QAAAAJ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> ranging from hospital ranking methodology, survey interviewer fraud, and new technology and data sources for social science research. He has published two books: ''Social Media, Sociality, and Survey Research''<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Hill |first1=Craig |title=Social Media, Sociality, and Survey Research |last2=Dean |first2=Elizabeth |last3=Murphy |first3=Joe |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2013 |isbn=978-1-118-37973-8}}</ref> and ''Big Data Meets Survey Science: A Collection of Innovative Methods''.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781118976357 |title=Big Data Meets Survey Science: A Collection of Innovative Methods |date=2020-10-13 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-1-118-97632-6 |editor-last=Hill |editor-first=Craig A. |edition=1 |language=en |doi=10.1002/9781118976357 |s2cid=240797608 |editor-last2=Biemer |editor-first2=Paul P. |editor-last3=Buskirk |editor-first3=Trent D. |editor-last4=Japec |editor-first4=Lilli |editor-last5=Kirchner |editor-first5=Antje |editor-last6=Kolenikov |editor-first6=Stas |editor-last7=Lyberg |editor-first7=Lars E. |access-date=2024-02-09 |archive-date=2023-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107040354/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781118976357 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Until July 2024, he was Senior Vice President at [[RTI International]] for more than 20 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Craig Hill |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/craigahill22/ |website=LinkedIn |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref> Prior to RTI, he was a vice president at [[NORC at the University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BigSurv2023 Academic {{sic|Co|mittee|nolink=y}} {{!}} BigSurv |url=https://www.bigsurv.org/Academic%20Committee |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=www.bigsurv.org |archive-date=2024-01-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240119221020/https://www.bigsurv.org/Academic%20Committee |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Recognition ==
In 2019, he was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASA Fellows |url=https://www.amstat.org/ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=American Statistical Association |archive-date=1996-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19961028041102/https://www.amstat.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2021, he received the Warren J. Mitofsky Innovators Award from the [[American Association for Public Opinion Research]] for founding the [[Survey methodology#The role of big data|Big Data Meets Survey Science]] (BigSurv) initiative.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-07 |title=2021 Award Winners - Warren J. Mitofsky Innovators Award |url=https://aapor.org/past-conferences/2021-award-winners/ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=American Association for Public Opinion Research |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-12-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204071728/https://aapor.org/past-conferences/2021-award-winners/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
